First, we compute ${C}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{2} & =C\cdot C \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${C}^{2}=C,$ so $C$ is an idempotent matrix.

We can use this fact to compute ${C}^{3}$ quickly, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{C}^{3} & ={C}^{2}\cdot C \\  & =C\cdot C \\  & ={C}^{2} \\  & =C\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
{C}^{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$
